description:
## Why

The current soft-cap implementation in FsBlockStore calls dir_bytes_used() — an O(n) readdir + stat scan — before every put when max_bytes is set. This is filesystem-specific and gets slow at scale (100k+ blocks).

## What

Move quota accounting into a SQLite row (backend_quota table: backend_id, total_bytes). The IpfsBlockStore trait already abstracts storage; quota tracking should live above it, not inside each implementation.

Hot path becomes O(1): check row, write block, increment row.

## Design

- Add backend_quota table: (backend_id TEXT PK, total_bytes INTEGER)
- On startup: scan the actual backend once to reconcile the row (pays O(n) cost once, not per-write)
- On put: check row against cap, write block, increment row
- On delete: decrement row
- Accept soft-cap semantics: a crash between write and row update leaves a small undercount, which is fine

## Acceptance

- FsBlockStore no longer calls dir_bytes_used() on the hot write path
- Quota check works identically for fs, LMDB, S3, and any future backend
- Startup reconciliation resets the row to the true byte count
notes: dir_bytes_used() is in crates/reader/src/post/fs_store.rs. The same pattern would apply to crates/transit/src/peering/fs_store.rs.
title: Track block store quota in SQLite row, not per-backend scan
